title: DEVELOPMENT OF E-/W-BAND SLOW WAVE STRUCTURE BREAD BOARDS FOR HIGH POWER TWTS EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop a E-/W-band traveling wave tube slow-wave structure breadboard capable of delivering 100 W of output power.Description: The millimetre wave domain is also known as the extremely high-frequency (EHF) spectrum ranges from 30 to 300 GHz. Early works on atmospheric propagation in EHF evidenced encouraging future usage for satellite communications. The allocated W-band for satellite services (71-76 GHz and 81-86 GHz) potentially provides a favourable attenuation window due to low oxygen absorption. The exploitation of W-band may offer broad bandwidths for high data rate information transfer. Hence the development of the high power amplifiers is a critical building block that acts as an enabler to exploit this frequency band for satellite telecommunications. Currently, solid state power amplifiers cover this frequency band, but with output powers significantly lower than 100 W and very low efficiency. A traveling wave tube amplifier (TWTA) solution offers better performance in terms of output power and efficiency. This activity aims at developing a traveling wave tube slow-wave structure in W-band, capable of delivering 100 W of output power. As a result of the validation of this key building block, European industry will gain crucial knowledge and pass a first important milestoneon their way to design and manufacture full TWTs in this frequency band. At present, no W-band space TWTs are available in Europe. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Design a traveling wave tube slow-wave structure in W-band, capable of delivering 100 W of output power - Manufacturing of a breadboard - Testing and validation of a breadboardDeliverables: Breadboard, Report

title: LISA-ITT-041 Thermal & Contamination Protection System
description:
The gravitational wave observatory LISA (Laser Interferometer Space Antenna) has been selected as ESA’s third large class mission (L-3) within the Cosmic Vision programme. LISA’s mission objective is to observe gravitational waves from space in the frequency band of 0.1 mHz to 1 Hz, not accessible from ground-based observatories. 
The mission architecture consists of a constellation of three spacecraft placed at the vertexes of a near-equilateral triangle with side length of about 2.5 million km (LISA Constellation). An overview of the LISA mission and its objectives can be found on the Agency website here: https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Space_Science/LISA
OHB, prime contractor for the programme, has been contracted by the European Space Agency (ESA) for the realization of the LISA programme, building the industrial consortium.
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the subcontractor for the LISA Core Assembly Thermal and Contamination Protection (LCA TCP) System.
The LCA TCP System’s primary function is to thermally decouple critical components within LCA from LISA platform. Secondary function is the protection of these same components from both particle and light contamination. TCP System is considered critical for achieving and maintaining the required performance of the LISA payload throughout the mission, by creating and maintaining specified operational environment within the LCA both on ground and in orbit.
The procurement of the LCA Thermal and Contamination Protection System will be conducted in line with the “ESA Best Practices for the Selection of Subcontractors by Prime Contractors in the frame of ESA’s Major Procurements. Additional requirements on geo-return may be specified in the ITT data package.

title: Service Contract for the Security Services at OSF and AOS in ALMA Observatory, at Paranal Observatory, La Silla Observatory and at ESO Premises in Vitacura.
description: Division: ALMA/DOO. Preliminary Inquiry (PI) to identify and select companies that are interested in and capable of providing security services for the ALMA Observatory, located 18 km from San Pedro de Atacama, for the ESO Paranal Observatory, located 130 km south of Antofagasta, for the ESO La Silla Observatory located 160 km north of La Serena and for the ESO Premises located at Vitacura, in Chile. The scope of the services includes: For ALMA, the scope of the services primarily covers a 24 hr/day access control at the main entrance on the public road CH23, the base camp buildings and main access gate to the high site, at buildings and secondary access to the ALMA high site (at 5,000 meters above sea level) and regular patrolling of the site. For Paranal, the scope of the services primarily includes a 24 hr/day access control and a 12 hr/night shift patrol on the Observatory site. For La Silla, the scope is primarily the security of the site at night. For Vitacura, the scope of the services includes a 24 hr/day access control at the entrance gate. The services dedicated to ALMA, Paranal and Vitacura shall start on 1 December 2022 for a period of 31 months with options to extend it by up to 24 months more. The services dedicated to La Silla shall start on 1 July 2022 for a period of 36 months with options to extend it by up to 24 months more. The PI will be released in Q3/2021 to potential suppliers in Chile and will be followed by a Call for tender planned to be issued in Q4/2021. The contract is expected to be awarded in Q2/2022, to the bidder, which has submitted a fully compliant tender and offers the best value for money for ESO taking into account the quality and price of the offer. title: FIRST!7 STRUCTURES, MATERIALS, MECHANISMS AND PROCESSES FOR SPACE TRANSPORTATION - EXPRO+
description: This ITT targets short-term, quick maturation of disruptive technologies across five categories of interest:A.Optimised materialsfor composite and/or metallic structures: technologies that bring significant performance improvements in terms of mass, robustnessor sustainability like (but not limited to) vitrimers, nanocomposites, new resins, fibers, metallic alloys, including Europeanization of alloys or key materialsB.Optimised processes for composite or metallic structures: technologies that bring significant improvement in terms of recurring costs or sustainability. It would include (but not only) new winding techniques, thermoplastic welding,advanced manufacturing like AFSW and DED, resin fiber moulding, repair and online inspection techniques. In that topic, full automation and increasing role of AI could be of highest interest for disruptive improvementC.Disruptive composite technologies for Space Transportation in cryogenic environment: the compatibility of composite materials with cryogenic substances (propellants in particular) is a major issue, and being able to easily store cryo fluids in composite structures can bring significant performance gains. Proposed technologies can cover cryogenic linerless composites tank, cleaning processes, innovative structural junctions, interfacesfor fluidic element and sealing for CFRP cryogenic tanks. The above list is not exhaustiveD.Electro-Mechanical Space Transportation structures: like (but not limited to) technologies that allow quick and efficient health check for reusable structures or in-orbit structure. It can also include multi-functional structures like integrated raceways, structural energy systems and structural actuatorsE.Mechanisms for space transportation systems: Deployment, releasing, locking or grabbing mechanisms are key for new space transportation systems like reusable structures or OTVs. The existing technologies are often complex, heavy and expensive. This category aims at proposing disruption in this matterParallel contract, 1 @500kEUR and 1@1 MEUR per category, are contemplated, the number and value of which may vary depending on the interest of the proposals, and availability of the respective nationality budgets.

title: LIBIN - Euro Space center : création d'une plate-forme web en vue de valoriser les métiers en lien avec les missions spatiales
description: Le présent marché porte sur la conception et la réalisation d’une plateforme web visant à valoriser les métiers en lien avec les missions spatiales. L’objectif est de proposer une « exposition virtuelle » attractive et interactive, intégrant la charte graphique de l’Euro Space Center et orientée vers un public d’adolescents et leurs usages web actuels. Le pouvoir adjudicateur sollicite le soumissionnaire pour la remise d’une offre de prestations comprenant la gestion complète du projet à savoir les tâches de conception et réalisation de la plateforme web, la conception de l’expérience de visite, le graphisme, la création et l’intégration de contenus numériques avec optimisation SEO, la traduction des contenus (FR, NL, EN, DE), d’hébergement, de testing et de mise en production du nouveau site ainsi que sa maintenance et ses développements futurs éventuels pour une durée de 4 ans.
